result.scope_note: Idempotent methods in HTTP semantics include GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and PUT; safe methods include GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS. The intersection of safe and idempotent depends on the specific standard's definitions.

explanation.text: The claim is false because it states 'every safe HTTP request method is idempotent' whereas the standard (RFC 2616) defines only GET and HEAD as safe, and additionally classifies GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE as idempotent. The claim's scope of 'every safe HTTP request method' does not map

to the set of all idempotent methods; safe methods are a subset limited to GET and HEAD, which are idempotent, but the claim incorrectly implies all safe methods (GET and HEAD) are the only idempotent ones or that the standard defines a 'June 2022 standard used worldwide' not established.
No evidence was found for a June 2022 standard used worldwide; both sources reference historic RFC 2616, not a 2022 edition with global usage.

assessment.rationale: Span 18 quotes the HTTP RFC 2616 section on idempotence: 'Methods can also have the property of idempotence... The methods GET, HEAD, PUT and DELETE share this property. Also, the methods OPTIONS and TRACE should not have side effects, and so are inherently idempotent.' Span 19 defines GET and HEAD.
assessment.provenance_note: HTTP RFC 2616 defines idempotent methods as GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE; safe methods as GET, HEAD; POST and PATCH are explicitly not idempotent or safe.
limitations: Only covers RFC 2616, not the June 2022 standard specifically

excerpts.text:
*"Methods can also have the property of “idempotence” in that (aside from error or expiration issues) the side-effects of N > 0 identical requests is the same as for a single request. The methods* `GET`*,* `HEAD`*,* `PUT` *and* `DELETE` *share this property. Also, the methods* `OPTIONS` *and* `TRACE` *should not have side effects, and so are inherently idempotent."*

`GET` and `HEAD` operations are additionally [defined as ‘safe’](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2616#section-9.1.1) which means they should have no side effects and thus should not have the significance of taking an action other than retrieval.
